correctness.rationale: The degree-three point-vanishing ideal is the space of alternating Frobenius cubics, whose nonsingular members form one GL4(F2) orbit; a rank-two cubic cannot cut out a smooth complete intersection with any quartic because the singular projective line meets the quartic. Exact 15-point evaluation yields a 20-dimensional quartic kernel and its 16-dimensional quotient modulo G times linear forms. Full 65536-class orbit and rational-gradient enumeration leaves exactly two Sp4(F2) orbits of size 144. Four-chart exact Gröbner bases certify the good orbit geometrically smooth, and an explicit degree-five singular point excludes the other. An exact group traversal verifies Sp4 order 720 and stabilizer order 5; the 28 nondegenerate alternating cubics yield 4032 embedded curves in one PGL4 orbit. A genuine order-five matrix preserving the ideal has four primitive-eigenline fixed points lying on the curve. Adjunction and tame Riemann–Hurwitz prove genus 19, genus-three quotient and four branch points. Computation paths are self-contained in the included package; finite enumeration is exhaustive only for the specified binary parameter space.

value.rationale: Uniqueness up to all ambient projective transformations is a natural moduli/classification question not resolved by the previously counted 144 fixed-cubic equations. The stabilizer C5 is a substantive symmetry restriction, not a paraphrase of a count, and its explicit fixed-point calculation exhibits every such minimal embedded genus-19 example as a tame cyclic cover of a genus-three curve with a four-point Frobenius-conjugate branch locus. This links the finite space-filling construction to lower-genus covering geometry and gives a canonical projective isomorphism type and reproducible classification invariant. The claim is not an arbitrary parameter slice: it covers the entire smallest complete-intersection family over F2.
